# ethereum-optimism/docs Weekly Report (Jan 4 - 10, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week's activity was centered on deep analysis and triage of critical issues rather than shipping new features. Significant effort was dedicated to investigating the root causes of L2 reorgs in Kona, with detailed analysis identifying multiple contributing factors in the L1 Origin Selector and block building logic. Concurrently, a strong push was made to improve documentation quality and developer experience, with several new pull requests opened to add content and a new issue created to standardize contribution processes. Discussions also highlighted dependencies on the supernode for resolving issues related to reporting and the `op-challenger`.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no major features or bug fixes were completed this week, several pull requests were opened to enhance project documentation and developer resources:

*   **Governance and Event Documentation:** New content was proposed, including a page for an U18 notice ([#1940](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1940)), an "Ethereum Ohio" event page ([#1937](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1937)), and updates to the governance FAQ concerning S9 Citizenship selections ([#1939](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1939)).
*   **Developer Tooling Documentation:** To improve the developer experience, a pull request was submitted to enhance the sample code for the Actions SDK Configuration ([#1934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1934)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
Issue management focused on diagnosing complex system behavior, clarifying documentation, and planning future work.

*   **Closed Issues:**
    *   An issue regarding OP Stack compatibility with minimal Base-style contracts ([#18709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18709)) was closed, with confirmation that smart contracts generally work as expected and a reference to existing documentation on differences from L1.

*   **New & Active Issues:**
    *   **Kona Stability:** A significant portion of the week's focus was on Kona. A detailed root cause analysis for L2 reorgs due to L1 reorgs ([#18676](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18676)) identified caching issues and missing validation steps. Related discussions continued on revising the `SyncStatus CurrentL1` selection logic ([#18673](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18673)), and a new contributor expressed interest in adding Kona support to `TestSequencerPreset` ([#18675](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18675)).
    *   **Supernode Dependencies:** Progress on several issues was noted as being dependent on supernode development. These include issues with supernode reporting and consistency ([#18651](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18651), [#18667](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18667)) and updating the `op-challenger` vm-runner ([#18669](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18669)), which requires a `syncStatus` API.
    *   **Documentation & DX Improvements:** Several new issues were opened to improve documentation clarity and process. These include correcting a mismatched description for a batcher configuration variable ([#1933](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/1933)), clarifying database paths ([#1935](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/1935)), proposing a new landing page ([#1936](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/1936)), and adding a PR title requirement to standardize contributions ([#1938](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/1938)).
    *   **Ongoing Bug Investigations:** The critical `eth_simulatev1` error post-Jovian fork ([#739](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/739)) saw an update, noting that a fix is in progress in the `op-geth` repository. Additionally, the issue to extend the `IDisputeGame` interface ([#18516](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18516)) was reopened to address remaining TODOs in the codebase.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week saw strong engagement from the contributor community, with several individuals proactively offering to take on complex issues. DeborahOlaboye requested assignment for fixing Pectra rollup config field generation ([#14816](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/14816)) and re-enabling flaky acceptance tests ([#16972](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/16972)). Similarly, crStiv expressed interest in tackling Kona support for sequencer tests ([#18675](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/issues/18675)). This proactive involvement, coupled with detailed discussions and clarifications from maintainers like pauldowman and op-will, highlights a healthy and collaborative development environment.
